youtube.title: WEEKLY ROUNDUP
youtube.summary: Dieuwe de Boer and William McGimpsey break down a flurry of election-season immigration announcements, from NZ First's citizenship and deportation reforms to Labour's residency changes and Pauline Hanson's revised One Nation target in Australia. They also examine the Act Party's push to wind up the Waitangi Tribunal, before closing with reflections on Trump-era comments touching Irish reunification and the Israel-Palestine settlements row.

youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: Steven Sykes joins Paul Brennan for Tech Tuesday, opening with mailbag questions on private VPN choices before CERN's switch away from IBM's Red Hat Linux. The main focus is Google's looming Android Developer Verification scheme, which threatens app sideloading and privacy, prompting a detailed case for de-Googled, GrapheneOS-based phones as a practical way to reclaim control, security and freedom from Big Tech's tightening grip. For everything you need to Say NO To Digital ID Stay on top of developments. G et RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: SALL GROVER
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Giggle for Girls founder Sal Grover after the High Court refused her special leave application, bringing the Tickle v Giggle case to a close in Australia. Sal reflects on the ruling, accuses the judiciary and Human Rights Commission of ideological capture and discusses the case's fallout for women's spaces, her mounting legal costs and her plans to potentially relaunch her platform overseas. To donate to the Giggle Crowd Fund Discover more from Sall on Facebook and X

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined from Melbourne by Tim Wilms, unpacking Australia's contentious digital duty of care legislation and the eSafety Commissioner's expanding powers. They also dig into the escalating feud between Andrew Hastie and Pauline Hanson, a High Court challenge from the White Australia Party, the Tickle vs Giggle fallout, scrapped AI seatbelt fines in Western Australia and a fatal Victorian pothole crash. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled Look beyond the headlines. G et RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Winston Peters joins Paul Brennan to defend New Zealand First's proposed 20,000 residency cap and referendum, arguing decades of immigration-driven demand have masked New Zealand's weak underlying economic growth. He also urges caution on AI regulation, dismisses ACT's crypto policy ambitions, and weighs in on the escalating Red Sea shipping crisis, rising borrowing costs, and this week's looming GDP figures. Discover more from Winston Peters on X , Facebook and Instagram For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: NAVIGATING THE CRAZY
youtube.summary: Gerry Pyves launches a new show Navigating the Crazy, with psychotherapist and AUT Professor Dr Keith Tudor. They explore how we navigate a confusing world by balancing our inner experience with external reality, questioning authority without rejecting it outright, avoiding echo chambers and finding purpose and meaning. They also discuss how early experiences shape our sense of self, the importance of knowing and accepting ourselves and the value of genuine human connection and open conversation. Discover more from Dr Keith Tudor and Gerry Pyves

youtube.title: CLAIRE BLEAKLEY & ELVIRA DOMMISSE
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with President of GE Free NZ Claire Bleakley and Dr Elvira Dommisse, former genetic engineering researcher, about 102 experimental pesticides, confidential field trials and concerns over the impact on organic farmers. They also discuss genetic engineering, patent-driven agriculture, the HSNO, Gene Technology and ACVM bills and urge the public to contact MPs ahead of their second reading on September 17.
